Photograph: Ben A Pruchnie/Getty Top Gear BBC to bring back Top Gear amid speculation about show’s next presenters Motoring series to return four years after Andrew ‘Freddie’ Flintoff suffered serious injuries in crash during filming Caroline Davies Thu 27 Aug 2026 10.32 EDT First published on Thu 27 Aug 2026 07.58 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google Top Gear, the long-running motoring show that has been off air since its co-host Andrew “Freddie” Flintoff was seriously injured in a crash during filming almost four years ago, is to return to the BBC, the broadcaster has confirmed. After Flintoff’s accident at Dunsfold aerodrome in Surrey, the BBC said the series would be “rested” for the foreseeable future. The BBC’s director of entertainment, Ed Havard, confirmed the news of its return at a panel event at the Edinburgh TV festival on Thursday. “There has been a lot of speculation about this and we can confirm that Top Gear is coming back,” he said. Havard refused to be drawn on who would host the show amid reports that the comedian and presenter – and a known car enthusiast – Jimmy Carr was in the frame. “I’m not going to talk about talent today,” he replied to questions. “Jimmy would be a great host but I won’t be discussing that today. “We will have more information on Top Gear shortly,” Havard added. Carr was a guest on Top Gear in 2004, and has said: “It’s one of the biggest shows in the world. It’s a global phenomenon.” The former England rugby player and Celebrity Traitors star Joe Marler is also reportedly being considered to host. View image in fullscreen The former England rugby player Joe Marler’s name has been mooted as a possible presenter. Photograph: Ian West/PA The model Jodie Kidd is another rumoured contender. Kidd has appeared on Top Gear in the past, and after qualifying for a racing licence, began racing in Italy. She has also hosted various automotive shows including Channel 5’s The Classic Car Show, Chubb Insurance’s classic car podcast, and her own YouTube channel, Kidd in a Sweet Shop. View image in fullscreen Jodie Kidd taking part in a rally in Brescia, Italy, in 2014. Photograph: Olycom SPA/Rex Others who have featured in speculation include the celebrity chef Gordon Ramsay, who has appeared on Top Gear several times and owns an extensive collection of cars, and the actor Rowan Atkinson, another car enthusiast who appeared during series 17, where he set a lap time of 1min 42.2sec, making him the fastest celebrity on the leaderboard at the time. Top Gear began in 1977 and became one of the BBC’s biggest hits in the hands of Jeremy Clarkson, Richard Hammond and James May in the 2000s. Clarkson’s contract was not renewed at the end of the 22nd season, after he punched a producer. He later issued a formal apology . Clarkson’s co-hosts also left after his departure, with the trio then signing up for another motoring show, The Grand Tour, on Amazon Prime Video. They were replaced by the broadcaster Chris Evans and the Friends star Matt LeBlanc. Evans left after just six episodes. The show also received criticism after LeBlanc and a rally driver performed “doughnuts” near the Cenotaph war memorial in London’s Whitehall. View image in fullscreen Paddy McGuinness, Chris Harris and Andrew ‘Freddie’ Flintoff. Photograph: Lee Brimble/PA Flintoff, Paddy McGuinness and Chris Harris took over in 2018. Flintoff was taken to hospital with facial and rib injuries when the Morgan Super 3 he was driving – an open-topped three-wheeled car – flipped upside down and skidded on the tarmac before coming to a stop. The BBC later reached a financial settlement with the England cricket captain, an agreement reportedly worth about £9m . He has revealed he was deeply affected by the crash and did not leave his house for six months other than to attend medical appointments. View image in fullscreen Flintoff has said he suffers from PTSD as a result of the Top Gear crash. Photograph: Gareth Copley/Getty In the Disney+ documentary Flintoff, released last year, the presenter admitted that after the accident, he did not think he had it in him to “get through”. Flintoff said his then three-and-a-half-year-old son Preston “wouldn’t come near me”. “I think it frightened him, my face; it frightened me. That was heartbreaking,” he said in the documentary. “I’ve got PTSD [post-traumatic stress disorder] and I get anxious, for periods of time. I just find myself crying for no particular reason.” Flintoff also said he relived the crash every night when he went to bed and described the experience as a “vivid” movie. https://www.dw.com/en/german-bundeswehr-.text: Skip to content Skip to main menu Skip to more DW sites https://p.dw.com/p/5NpYc Emden on the North Sea will be a naval city again Image: Sina Schuldt/dpa/picture alliance Advertisement After months of evaluating different locations, German Defense Minister Boris Pistorius has announced that the Bundeswehr 's new naval port will be built in Emden, on the North Sea coast of Lower Saxony . "Emden offers ideal conditions, such as quick access to the Atlantic Ocean and the far north," Pistorius said. He added that a second port is needed to accommodate the growing German Navy : New ships and boats require berths, and additional service members need housing. Furthermore, he said, "this will enhance the deterrence capabilities of both Germany and NATO ." The commercial port of Emden is the economic heart of East Frisia. Not only does it dominate the cityscape, but it also provides thousands of jobs. Directly adjacent to the port is the large Volkswagen plant, from which cars are exported by ship to destinations around the world. The port also serves as a shipment hub for large components for wind farms in the North Sea. Now, a naval base with up to 2,000 military posts will be built by the early 2030s. Emden hosted a Bundeswehr base until 1997, but it was no longer needed after the end of the Cold War and was consequently decommissioned. Boris Pistorius announced the plans for a new naval port in Emden Image: Sina Schuldt/dpa/picture alliance Emden's 'great advantage' Coastal land is tough to come by in Germany, but that's not the case in Emden. The port city has "the great advantage of having a lot of available space where a new port can be developed," says Johannes Peters, an expert on maritime security at the Institute for Security Policy at the University of Kiel. "Emden offers the opportunity to build a dedicated naval port that complies with the latest requirements, including those for security and port protection," Peters emphasizes in an interview with DW. Pistorius estimates that up to 450 hectares of land will be needed — equivalent to about 630 soccer fields. The only naval port currently on the German North Sea coast is located in Wilhelmshaven. From a strategic perspective, it doesn't make sense to have just one port and nothing to fall back on, security expert Peters emphasized. "If some kind of scenario where conflict breaks out were to actually occur and this infrastructure were to fail, then you'd have a real problem. That's why they want to diversify their options here now." Pistorius said there was a strategic advantage to a second naval port on the North Sea: "This makes us harder to predict in an emergency and expands our operational capabilities." Relief for Wilhelmshaven The planned port in Emden is intended to complement and provide relief for the Wilhelmshaven naval base. This is where Operational Flotilla 2 is stationed, a large formation consisting of frigates and supply ships. The Wilhelmshaven naval base is also being expanded as the fleet grows and personnel levels increase. In reference to Wilhelmshaven, Pistorius said the "smallest navy in the history of the Bundeswehr" now had more responsibilities than ever before. "So the navy must grow, and it will," P{istorius said. "We have laid the groundwork for this in all areas." German rearmament sparks controversy, again To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video Bremerhaven was also on the shortlist. Although it will not be getting a naval base, the German government is investing a great deal of money there as well. The port will be expanded into a logistical hub that could be used to deploy large troop contingents and heavy equipment from NATO allies in the event of an emergency. That is the plan outlined in "Operation Plan Germany," Germany's defense plan in the event of a crisis or threat to alliance security. The federal government is allocating up to €1.35 billion ($1.51 billion) for the expansion. Jobs for Emden? Although Emden has been officially chosen as the site, so far this is only a memorandum of understanding between the Defense Ministry, the state of Lower Saxony and the city of Emden. Construction of the naval port is likely to take years. "There are still major hurdles to overcome," says Defense Minister Pistorius. "You can't just walk into a home improvement store and buy a new naval base," Pistorius said. "Marine engineering, transportation links, the barracks — we need to get started on these right away." The city, with its approximately 50,000 residents, is expected to benefit from the construction of the port, especially since the future of the local Volkswagen plant is uncertain because of ongoing economic trouble for the automaker. Mayor Tim Kruithoff was all the more delighted. "This is a great day for Emden," he said. He called the planned naval base "an extraordinary opportunity" for jobs and for the economic development of the entire region. This article was originally written in German. https://cyprus-mail.com/2026/10/11/polis.text: Polish security services convened a special meeting on Sunday after receiving information about a potential attack on Prime Minister Donald Tusk and Defence Minister Wladyslaw Kosiniak-Kamysz, an Interior Ministry spokesperson said on X. The exact nature of the threat and its origin were not immediately clear. “Following information received by the Polish Police regarding a possible attack …Interior Minister, Marcin Kierwiński, and the Minister-Coordinator of Special Services, Tomasz Siemoniak, have ordered action to be taken in this matter,” spokesperson Karolina Galecka wrote. “A meeting will be held today at 11:00 a.m. at the Internal Security Agency’s Counter-Terrorism Centre.” A spokesperson for the minister-coordinator of special services said he had no further comment. Private broadcaster Radio Zet reported that police had received an email with information about the threat. While violent crime is relatively rare in Poland, the country is deeply polarised politically and has faced security threats due to its proximity to the war in Ukraine. In August, police detained a 23-year-old man accused of calling for the assassination of senior Polish politicians. In 2024, Tusk said he received threats after an assassination attempt on Slovak Prime Minister Robert Fico. Sunday’s announcement came as authorities in Poland have been on high alert following a wave of violence in schools that resulted in the death of a caretaker on Thursday.

https://www.liverpoolecho.co.uk/travel/n.text: Twinkling lights, steaming mulled wine and the smell of sizzling bratwursts are all part of the appeal of a traditional Christmas market . But finding one filled with local crafts rather than mass-produced souvenirs can be harder than it sounds. These six festive destinations across England, Northern Ireland and mainland Europe offer Christmas atmosphere, handcrafted gifts and traditional winter food. GetYourGuide travel expert Maren Schullerus shares some advice for shoppers hoping to avoid tourist traps: "When it comes to souvenir buying, there's a few indicators that the person has made it themselves, as opposed to it being shipped from a factory. "Three tips: Look for stalls that won't let you photograph their crafts, look for tradespeople that can tell you how they made it, and make sure you're allowed to pick it up and have a look before you buy it." Best for: Medieval atmosphere Dates: 18 November to 22 December Chester's historic walls, Gothic cathedral and distinctive black-and-white timber-framed buildings make a picturesque backdrop for its Christmas market. A brightly lit Christmas tree stands among traditional wooden chalets, where traders from across the North West sell regional cheeses, handmade fudge, gin, silver jewellery, candles and handcrafted soaps. The market is more compact than some of its counterparts, but there is plenty more shopping nearby. The Rows, Chester's historic covered shopping galleries, are home to independent boutiques. The market opens seven days a week, closing at 6.30pm from Sunday to Wednesday and 8pm from Thursday to Saturday. Hog roasts, real ales and mulled wine provide plenty of options for refreshments. Another festive highlight is the Winter Watch Parade, a historic revival featuring medieval and Renaissance characters, Roman soldiers and fire-breathers making their way through the streets. Chester Castle also hosts medieval-themed seasonal events with traditional live music and an appearance by St Nicholas. Best for: Christmas spirit Dates: 20 November to 6 January, including Christmas Day Tallinn's UNESCO World Heritage Old Town provides a fairytale setting, with cobbled streets, medieval buildings and a daily arrival by Father Christmas on his reindeer-drawn sleigh. The city has displayed a fir tree outside its town hall since 1441, a tradition described as Europe's first public Christmas tree. Browse locally made linen textiles, felted wool items, knitwear and wooden crafts, then sample Estonian favourites including blood sausages, sauerkraut and gingerbread. Warm up with glogg, a hot spiced wine fortified with spirits and made with local buckthorn berries, before taking a ride on the traditional carousel or a turn on the ice rink. The market opens daily from 10am to 8pm. Hot drinks are served until 10pm, with later hours at weekends. Allow time to explore the city's cafés, museums and public saunas. Adventurous visitors can also try winter swimming. Best for: Regional and international food Dates: 14 November to 22 December Belfast is an accessible and often affordable option for a festive break. Against the backdrop of City Hall, traditional German-style chalets offer handcrafted gifts and a wide choice of food. Expect exotic meat burgers, Dutch pancakes, Italian chocolates, speciality cheeses and steaming mugs of glühwein. Families can also enjoy a vintage fairground and Santa's Grotto. The market closes at 8pm from Monday to Wednesday, with stalls and beer tents staying open later from Thursday onwards. Rory King, founder of Rory's Travel Club, says: "One of the best things is the mix of local and international food. Rather than sitting down for one big meal, I'd share a few things and try as much as possible. My favourite pick is the crumble stall where you DIY your own crumble and custard dessert! "Local traders make up over half of the stalls, so you can pick up an authentic souvenir. It's very busy in the evenings and Saturdays, so I'd go during the day for the food and shopping , then come back later for a drink and to see City Hall lit up. "Give yourself at least one night in Belfast – spend a couple of hours at the Christmas market, but also visit Cathedral Quarter and St George's Market." Best for: Christmas on a budget Dates: 13 November to 1 January, with both main markets open on Christmas Day Budapest offers two main festive attractions: Advent Basilica in St Stephen's Square and the Christmas market in Vorosmarty Square. Smaller markets are scattered throughout the city too. Although Christmas market prices can be higher than elsewhere, Budapest remains a relatively affordable destination. A mulled wine costs roughly half what you would pay in Austria or Germany. At Advent Basilica, a nightly light show illuminates the basilica's façade above an ice rink and stalls selling Hungarian ceramics, jewellery and leatherwork. A 10-minute walk away, Vorosmarty Square hosts the city's oldest Christmas market. Visitors can browse local crafts, listen to live music and try Hungarian treats such as kurtoskalacs, or chimney cake, and Kolbasz sausages. A nativity display and towering fir tree complete the festive scene. Beyond the markets, Budapest's thermal spas are a highlight. The historic Rudas baths beside the Danube offer views across the city from warm mineral water – particularly atmospheric when it snows. Best for: A quick hop across the Channel Dates: 18 November to 30 December, closed on Christmas Day A Eurostar journey of just one hour and 22 minutes from London St Pancras puts Lille within easy reach for a festive day trip. The market is a 10-minute walk from the station, where mulled wine, cheesy tartiflette and chocolate waffles await. The birthplace of Charles de Gaulle and historic former capital of Flanders, Lille is known for its Flemish-baroque architecture, made even more striking by Christmas illuminations. Its market has been a fixture in the city centre for more than 30 years. Wooden chalets sell regional produce, crafts, vintage toys, decorations and candles, with a towering Christmas tree and Ferris wheel adding to the atmosphere. The market stays open until 8.30pm on weekdays and 10pm at weekends. Afterwards, explore the historic patisseries and boulangeries along Lille's narrow, cobbled streets. Best for: Artisan gifts Dates: 20 November to 22 December Celebrating its 20th year, Winchester Cathedral Christmas market combines wooden chalets, twinkling lights, carols and mulled wine within the cathedral's historic Close. Carefully selected traders offer handcrafted gifts, artisan food and festive treats. The ice rink has not returned since the pandemic, but a food court provides plenty of seasonal dishes. Weekends can be particularly busy, so consider visiting during the week or travelling by train if you are happy to walk from the station. The market closes at 6pm on weekdays and 8pm at weekends. Winchester, England's ancient first capital, is worth exploring beyond the market. If your visit coincides with a Christmas cathedral service, hearing its world-renowned choir could provide a memorable finish to your festive break.
